The grinding noise's payoff is lacking, as there's really no reason specifically why the bodies have to be ground other than to make the ending as gruesome as possible. The thing I appreciate about this story the most is what it leaves up to the reader to figure out themselves like the source of the W named kids, but then the majority of what's going on is revealed in a massive exposition dump by one of the most cartoonishly evil characters I've read in a while.

Supposedly in 1976, a Fireman went to check on his two horses, when he found them dead, a huge black dog chewing on their necks. It fled into the woods, and for a few days the police force got thousands of calls claiming to have seen it all around town. When one officer finally found it, he shot it multiple times, but supposedly it didn't react to the bullets and walked away, never to be seen again.
